successors.name: Roman Republic
successors.text: Venetia from Lake Garda to the Tagliamento: Ateste, Patavium, Vicetia

ledger.x: c. 900 BC: Este I (c. 900-750 BCE), 'when the Veneti settle the Po Valley'; 'initially attested in the area between Lake Garda and the Euganean Hills', later 'borders similar to today's Veneto': Lake Garda, the Tartaro and Po to Adria, the Tagliamento. Cities Ateste, Patavium, Vicetia, Opitergium.

c. 400 BC: the Celtic Cenomani settle the Po plain west of the Veneti and 'eventually absorbed the areas of Brescia and Verona'; the page gives no year, so -400 is the cenomani dossier's placeholder (the cenomani found event names 'nobody').
c. 238 BC: the Veneti 'established amicitia with Rome against the Gauls'; friendship and alliance rather than subjection, so the tint is light.

89 BC: the Lex Pompeia de Transpadanis, 'promulgated by the Roman Consul Pompeius Strabo in 89 BC', gives Latin rights to the communities of Transpadana; the Veneti page puts the Veneti among them ('given Latin rights after the Social War in the Lex Pompeia de Transpadanis').
89 BC: Latin rights; the Venetic communities become Latin towns, then Roman citizens with the Lex Roscia (49 BC) and Regio X Venetia et Histria under Augustus.

certainty.note: Venetia between Lake Garda, the Po and the Tagliamento; Verona goes to the Cenomani from c.
